definitions.explanation: In baseball, a player who is sent in to run the bases in place of another player, typically to take advantage of superior speed.

examples.japanese: {代走|だいそう}を{送|おく}った。
examples.english: They sent in a pinch runner.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{速|はや}い{選手|せんしゅ}が{代走|だいそう}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: A fast player came in as a pinch runner.

examples.japanese: {監督|かんとく}は{九回|きゅうかい}{裏|うら}に{代走|だいそう}を{起用|きよう}して{盗塁|とうるい}を{狙|ねら}った。
examples.english: The manager put in a pinch runner in the bottom of the ninth to attempt a stolen base.

notes:
A baseball term composed of {代|だい} (substitute) and {走|そう} (run). Part of a family of baseball substitution terms that are commonly used in Japanese sports commentary.

RELATED BASEBALL SUBSTITUTION TERMS:
- {代打|だいだ}: pinch hitter — a substitute batter
- {代走|だいそう}: pinch runner — a substitute runner
- {代投|だいとう}: relief pitcher — a substitute pitcher (less common; {救援|きゅうえん}{投手|とうしゅ} is more standard)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {代走|だいそう}を{出|だ}す: to send in a pinch runner
- {代走|だいそう}に{出|で}る: to enter as a pinch runner
- {代走|だいそう}を{起用|きよう}する: to employ a pinch runner
- {代走|だいそう}{要員|よういん}: pinch runner specialist
